common_name: Angyo Star Fatshedera (White-Margined Star-Leaved Tree Ivy)

planting.note: Plant container-grown plants in spring in humus-rich, well-drained soil in shade to partial shade; Angyo Star holds its variegation well even in brighter light and grows noticeably faster than most other variegated Fatshedera selections.

directions: Selected at a Japanese nursery, Angyo Star carries wide creamy-white margins flecked with small green speckles around a rich green center, giving each star-shaped, palmately lobed leaf a two-toned frosted look distinct from the plain white edging of 'Variegata' or the central gold splash of 'Annemieke'. Unlike many variegated sports, it remains notably vigorous, pushing long semi-upright to sprawling stems that can be tied to a support for a small climbing accent or left loose as an informal shrub. Small rounded clusters of greenish-white flowers may appear on mature wood in autumn, but the plant is grown almost entirely for its foliage. Site it in humus-rich, well-drained soil in shade to bright partial shade, sheltered from hot midday sun that can scorch the pale margins, and prune only to shape or remove reverted all-green shoots.

planting.note: Plant container-grown plants in spring in humus-rich, well-drained soil in shade to partial shade; Curly stays more compact and lax-stemmed than the species, making it well suited to pots or small border spaces.

directions: Curly is an all-green sport of the Fatsia-ivy hybrid whose glossy, palmately lobed leaves twist and curl along their margins instead of lying flat, giving the plant a ruffled, textural look unlike any other Fatshedera selection. New spring growth often emerges with a chartreuse cast on burgundy-tinted stems before settling into deep green for the rest of the year. Its lax, viney stems stay shorter and denser than the species, so it works well trailing from a raised bed or large container as well as massed as a low shade groundcover. Grow it in humus-rich, well-drained soil in shade to partial shade, sheltered from hot sun and drying wind, and pinch stem tips occasionally to keep the habit full.
